name: GPU Robot Lab
description: Triton GPU kernels and a GPU robot simulation, benchmarked against PyTorch and a single CPU thread.
longDescription: Wrote Triton matrix-multiply kernels verified against PyTorch on an NVIDIA T4. Traced the slow first version to register spilling and tuned it 3.4x faster (1,096 to 3,727 GFLOPS), and found its compiled code uses no tensor cores, the likely cause of the remaining gap. Built a MuJoCo MJX robot simulation up to 126x faster than one CPU thread on a GPU (2.75x once collisions are added), with a planner 2 to 26x faster on the GPU than the CPU at the same batch size, and a neural-network controller, trained with a curriculum, that swings up and holds a pendulum. Ran controlled experiments: 10 repeats per version (PyTorch itself varied up to 44%), and a one-change-at-a-time test showing the grouped launch order adds 4 to 14%. Backed by 90+ automated tests in CI and an interactive explainer site on GitHub Pages.

name: InterviewPair
description: The core of an app that pairs students for mock technical interviews.
longDescription: Built the core of an app that pairs students for mock technical interviews: a Spring Boot API with JWT login, hashed passwords and a tested matching rule, and a React frontend, in one Docker image. Wrote 30+ automated tests, including expired, tampered and wrongly signed login tokens, and CI on GitHub Actions that builds the Docker image on every push.

name: Stock Price Prediction (AI4ALL Ignite, team project)
description: A 3-person team project predicting next-day stock decreases from financial news headlines.
longDescription: Contributed to a 3-person team project that predicts next-day stock decreases from financial news headlines, using FinBERT sentiment features and 20M+ stock price records. The Random Forest reached 54.4% accuracy against 50.8% for the Logistic Regression baseline on 64,599 held-out headlines. Wrote the evaluation script: 5-fold stratified cross-validation on a 50,000-article sample, with classification reports and confusion matrices for both models.
